en: The Triplet on the Visible, the Triplet on the Clung-to.

A non-visible, non-reacting state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-visible, non-reacting state that is acquired by clinging and subject to clinging.
(Abbreviated. There are six [conditions] in the case of the object; three in the case of the proximate, immediate, and decisive support;
six in the case of the prenascence; three in the case of the kamma, nutriment, and faculty; six in the case of presence; ... pe ... six in the case of non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is visible, impinging, not acquired by clinging, and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is visible, impinging, not acquired by clinging, and subject to clinging, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are twenty-one;
under predominance condition there are twenty-one … pe … under mutuality condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are twenty-one.

Conditioned by a state that is non-manifesting, impinging, not-clung-to, and not-liable-to-clinging, there arises a state that is non-manifesting, non-impinging, not-clung-to, and not-liable-to-clinging, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. There are three under root; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.
